summary: The deliverables mostly agree with their evidence. Five sentences say more than the evidence does or disagree between files: the room-ready time, 'the only real job', the 21,000 WebApp lines credited to the trial, '153 deploys', and 'the 59 P2 findings'. One gap changes the plan: from 2026-12-01 the account's monthly limit goes back to USD 300. Spend with no job behind it already runs about USD 9.30 a day, so December leaves room for about one or two jobs before every paid step is refused. Also, no existing US job carries the sharing statement, so a company that signs in today would still see nothing.

findings.today: Two things decide December. The month's limit goes back to USD 300. The host, Google Cloud and OpenAI cost with no job behind them already run about USD 9.30 a day, about USD 288 for the month. That leaves roughly USD 12 for every job in December. One job used USD 8.46. After one or two jobs the limit is reached. From then until January every new paid step is refused for every job. Each job waits for the next month, the site's page says the job is waiting on spending, and when its 7-day window passes the job ends held. Because the sound-free video waits for paid preparation (G-02), a job that waits like this never reaches a company. None of this is in the summary, the plan or the owner questions. Owner question 19 asks only which limits to delete.
findings.should: Before outreach starts, the owner knows how many jobs a month the account limit allows. Spend with no job behind it does not decide whether a site's job reaches companies.
findings.proposal: Owner step before wave 0's outreach: set the December limit with the fixed costs in view. Either keep USD 400 or more, or count only job spend against the limit and watch fixed costs with alerts alone. Add it to owner-questions.md as a money question with this arithmetic. In code, do PR 2.3 (sound-free video first, G-02) early so a money wait holds back only the simulation and not the listing. Deleting the idle lanes (V-01: the Cloud Run collector that starts about 1,180 times a day) should lower the Google Cloud line; measure it after the cut.
findings.user_result: A site that films in December still reaches companies, and the owner knows the month's job capacity in advance.
findings.risk: Raising the limit or narrowing what counts lets more money be spent. The per-job USD 40 cap and the provider limits still apply, and the owner decides. The OpenAI and Google Cloud lines with no job behind them may include development use that will fall. The USD 9.29 a day rests on 21.8 days of November.
findings.verify_how: Config read at HEAD and at the running release cbff06b. Spend figures read with operator_door.py status at 2026-11-22T20:13Z. Arithmetic shown in the evidence. That the limit actually stops a December job is inferred from the admission code and was not observed, because December has not started.

owner_questions.question: What should December's account limit be, and should fixed costs (the host, Google Cloud, development OpenAI use) count against the limit that stops site jobs?
owner_questions.recommendation: Count only job spend against the limit that refuses paid steps. Keep alerts on the whole bill. Otherwise keep USD 400 for December.
owner_questions.unblocks: K-01: more than one or two jobs in December.

not_covered: Sign-in, password reset, the site claim page (client/src/pages/ClaimSite.tsx) and /settings: not walked by any agent or by this check. A site needs no account, so no P0 or P1 conclusion rests on them.
Emails as sent (the HTML parts): no agent rendered them. Close by rendering each outbox kind from test fixtures with no send.
The Terms of Service read in full against the product: only the clauses behind M-01 and the price check were compared.
The Pipeline's functions/storage_trigger.py (the upload hand-off Cloud Function): mapped in inventory.md:1105 but not read for failure modes. extractFrames sits in a third repository.
Accessibility of the start form at phone width (labels, focus order, zoom, screen reader): not tested. Close with one axe run at 390 px on a local server.

A second or tenth job at the same time: only per-capture locks were found (website_atlas_pipeline.py:323, website_company_clip.py:546). Host throughput was not measured. The money limit (K-01) binds first.

The 14-day deletion of temporary processing files the Privacy Policy promises: the repository holds the bucket rule (pipeline:deploy/storage/primary-capture-bucket-lifecycle.json, Delete at age 14 for tmp/, staging/, debug/). Whether it is applied to the live bucket, and whether scratch files on the host follow it, was not read.
Deployed Firestore and Storage rules, and the values set in Render and on the host: still unread, as the audit already says.
